LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.6: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is Swimming an essential life skill?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner builds confidence by floating in water.

• Learning to learn: The learner acquires skills in swimming by practising water entry and floating in water.

Values:
• Respect: The learner respect others' performance in floating and gliding in water.

• Responsibility: The learner observes own and others safety while performing and practising the water entry, floatation and

gliding.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety and security: The learner adheres to water safety precautions while practising water entry, floatation and gliding.

• Environmental awareness: The learner familiarises on the pool environment and safe use of water and pool hygiene.

Link to other learning areas:

Integrated science: The learner develops a practical understanding of correct body posture when floating and gliding.

Suggested learning resources

Swimming pool, swimming costumes, floaters,
